newsitem.title: USA: In Texas, record $1.75 million illegal-worker fine.
newsitem.headline: In Texas, record $1.75 million illegal-worker fine.

text.p: A Texas restaurant chain was fined a record $1.75 million on Wednesday for violating U.S. immigration laws by employing illegal Mexican and Central American workers in its kitchens.

U.S. Attorney Paul Coggins said it was the largest fine ever imposed for immigration law violations in the workplace and came after the Houston-based Pappas chain pleaded guilty to four felony charges of shielding, concealing and harboring illegal aliens from detection.

Pappas Partners operates 54 restaurants under several names, including Pappadeaux Seafood Kitchen, Pappasito's Cantina and Pappas Bar-B-Q, but the investigation focused on six restaurants in the Dallas area.

The Immigration and Naturalization Service imposed the record fine after finding that Pappas had hired workers it knew to be illegal aliens, rehired them after they had been arrested or even deported and hid them from immigration agents during searches. The U.S. attorney's office helped the INS with its investigation.

"If you can't take the heat of prosecution, get your unauthorized workers out of the kitchen or any part of the workplace," Coggins said, adding that 80 illegal workers were found at a raid on Pappas restaurants in 1995 and 40 earlier this year.
INS Commissioner Doris Meissner called the case a landmark.
"This record fine sends a clear message that the Clinton administration will vigorously pursue those employers who violate immigration laws governing the American workplace," she said.
The INS has pledged to crack down on the employment of illegal immigrants, and the restaurant and hotel businesses are among its key targets.
Pappas said in a statement it had "taken action to prevent such occurrences in the future."
"We have instituted what is and what will be our course of action -- compliance with all necessary hiring standards and practices. We will tolerate nothing less," the firm said.
